difficultyRationale: Requires connecting a real-world bug (drifted validation rules) to the correct DRY remedy rather than a superficial workaround.
explanation: All three checks express the exact same knowledge: the product's single definition of a valid email address. Unlike code that merely looks similar but encodes different rules, this is genuine duplication of one rule, which is exactly the kind of drift DRY and a single source of truth are meant to prevent.

options.text: Leave the three copies as they are, but add a comment above each reminding future developers to update all three together.
options.explanation: Comments are not enforced by the compiler or by tests; this bug happened precisely because keeping three copies in sync relies on humans remembering, which a single source of truth is meant to eliminate by removing the duplication itself.

options.text: Keep the regex duplicated, but write a shared unit test that asserts all three regex strings are equal to each other.
options.explanation: This still leaves three independent copies of the same rule to maintain and only catches drift after the fact in a test, rather than removing the duplicated knowledge at its source.

options.text: Convert each regex to a named constant local to its own class, keeping three separate constants instead of three inline literals.
options.explanation: This improves local readability slightly but does not address the real problem: the same business rule is still implemented three times and can still drift, since the three constants are not guaranteed to stay equal.

options.text: Extract one shared EmailValidator.isValid(String email) method used by all three call sites.
options.explanation: All three checks encode the exact same knowledge: the product's definition of a valid email. Because this is genuine duplication of one rule rather than coincidentally similar code, giving it one authoritative implementation removes the drift risk that caused the bug.
